name: Interoperability of EU information systems (borders and visa) Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: implementation monitoring only; components not yet operating, so none of the outcome indicators can be measured; no independent studies
summary: The Regulation links the EU's border, visa and security databases so officials can check identities in one search and detect people using multiple identities. Delivery is about three years behind plan: the first component went live in May 2025 and the main search tools are due in June 2026, while spending by the EU IT agency alone (EUR 171 million) already exceeds the original one-off cost estimate. The promised savings and anti-fraud benefits cannot yet be measured.

indicators.indicator: Components ready for operations by target dates (search portal T0+36 months; common identity repository and multiple-identity detector end-2022/2023; shared biometric matching end-2023)
indicators.evidence: Far behind schedule: shared biometric matching service launched May 2025; European search portal and common identity repository due June 2026; multiple-identity detector in testing; reporting repository expected Q4 2026.

indicators.indicator: Number of searches handled by the European search portal vs total searches
indicators.evidence: Not yet operational in the reporting period.

indicators.indicator: Identities linked to the same biometrics; detected identity fraud cases
Number of step-1 (hit/no-hit) and step-2 accesses for law enforcement
Direct savings of EUR 77.5m a year, mostly for Member State administrations
indicators.evidence: Not measured; components not yet operating.

indicators.indicator: One-off cost EUR 169.8m (about half EU, half Member States); EUR 28.5m a year running costs
indicators.evidence: By 1 Dec 2025 eu-LISA alone had signed contracts worth EUR 170.8m for interoperability (EUR 133.2m paid), already above the whole one-off estimate for the EU and Member States combined.

literature.citation: European Commission (2017), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals on interoperability between EU information systems (executive summary SWD(2017) 474), SWD(2017) 473
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposals on interoperability between EU information systems (executive summary SWD(2017) 474)
literature.headline: Direct savings EUR 77.5m a year (training, resolving multiple identities); one-off costs EUR 169.8m, running costs EUR 28.5m a year; positive for border control and law enforcement
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected linking the EU's border and security databases to save national administrations about EUR 77.5 million a year for a one-off cost of about EUR 170 million.

literature.citation: European Commission (2026), Sixth report on the state of play of preparations for the full implementation of the Interoperability Regulations (covering 2025), COM(2026) 446
literature.title: Sixth report on the state of play of preparations for the full implementation of the Interoperability Regulations (covering 2025)
literature.headline: Shared biometric matching service launched 19 May 2025; Entry/Exit System rolled out 12 Oct 2025; search portal and common identity repository to start 12 June 2026; reporting repository Q4 2026; eu-LISA contracts EUR 170.8m signed, EUR 133.2m paid by Dec 2025
literature.summary_plain: Six years on, the first building block went live in 2025 and the rest is due in 2026, about three years later than planned, with spending already above the original estimate.

literature.citation: European Commission (2026), Report on the evaluation of eu-LISA under Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1726, COM(2026) 32 (SWD(2026) 980)
literature.title: Report on the evaluation of eu-LISA under Article 39 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1726
literature.headline: Operational management of existing systems effective, but development of new systems less so: contractor management, internal coordination and resource problems caused significant delays to EES, ETIAS, ECRIS-TCN and revised VIS; warns new tasks would raise the risk of further delays to the interoperability project
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's evaluation of the EU IT agency found it runs existing systems well but has struggled to deliver new ones on time, which has held up the interoperability project.
literature.quality: agency evaluation, not of the Regulation's effects
